description.en: One of Dallas's most iconic public spaces, Fair Park has served as a center for recreation, culture, and community since the city acquired it in 1904. Home to historic architecture, museums, and major events, the park continues to celebrate Dallas's rich history while welcoming generations of visitors.

Nestled in the historic Oak Cliff neighborhood, Lake Cliff Park has been a treasured gathering place since 1906. Known for its scenic lake, rose garden, historic pergola, and recreational amenities, the park blends natural beauty, thoughtful design, and more than a century of Dallas history.

Established through the generosity of Dr. W.W. Samuell, Samuell Grand Park is one of East Dallas's premier recreation destinations. Featuring athletic fields, aquatic facilities, an amphitheater, and open green spaces, the park continues its legacy of bringing the community together through sports, events, and outdoor recreation.

Reverchon Park is one of Dallas's oldest public parks, offering a unique blend of history, recreation, and natural beauty. Nestled along Turtle Creek, it features historic WPA stonework, scenic trails, a beloved baseball field, and direct access to the Katy Trail, making it a favorite destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

Established in 1876, City Park is Dallas's first municipal park and the birthplace of the city's park system. Originally designed as a scenic retreat, it has evolved into a vibrant community gathering place, reflecting nearly 150 years of Dallas history, recreation, and civic pride.

For more than a century, Pike Park has served as a cultural and community landmark just north of downtown Dallas. Closely tied to the city's Jewish and Mexican American heritage, the park has long provided a welcoming space for recreation, neighborhood gatherings, and community celebrations while preserving an important chapter of Dallas history.

Located in the Red Bird community, Thurgood Marshall Park has been a neighborhood gathering place since 1964. Home to Bahama Beach Family Water Park, a recreation center, athletic facilities, and Earl "Coach" Thompson Field, the park continues to foster recreation, youth development, and community connections.

name: Dallas Zoo

description.en: The Dallas Zoo is Texas' oldest and largest zoological park, spanning 106 acres and housing more than 2,000 animals from around the world. Since 1888, it has inspired generations through immersive wildlife habitats, conservation efforts, educational programs, and unforgettable experiences that connect visitors with the natural world.

streetAddress: 650 S. R.L. Thornton Fwy (I-35), Dallas, TX 75203

description.en: Established in 1919, Cedar Crest Golf Course is one of Dallas's most historic public golf destinations. Designed by renowned architect A.W. Tillinghast, the course has hosted prestigious championships, including the 1927 PGA Championship. Today, it continues to welcome golfers of all skill levels while preserving more than a century of Dallas golf history.

Established in 1915, Eloise Lundy Park is one of Dallas' oldest historic neighborhood parks and a landmark in the Tenth Street community. Once known as Oak Cliff Negro Park, it honors longtime Dallas Park and Recreation leader Eloise Lundy while continuing to serve as a center for recreation, culture, and community.

Crawford Memorial Park is a 266.2-acre southeast Dallas destination blending recreation, nature, and community connection. Featuring trails, athletic fields, picnic areas, public art, and preserved Blackland Prairie habitat, the park offers visitors opportunities to explore, gather, and experience the unique natural beauty of North Texas.

Bachman Lake Park is a 205-acre urban oasis offering scenic trails, water views, recreation, public art, and community amenities. From hiking and bike riding around the lake to skateboarding, swimming, and plane watching near Love Field Airport, the park provides a range of activities for Dallas residents and visitors.

Hattie R. Moore Park is a 3.6-acre West Dallas community space honoring the legacy of Hattie Rankin Moore, a dedicated advocate for children and families. The park reflects her commitment to service, providing a neighborhood gathering place focused on recreation, connection, and creating opportunities for future generations.

Juanita J. Craft Park is a 21.5-acre community park honoring one of Dallas's most influential civil rights leaders. Named for Juanita J. Craft, the "first lady of Dallas civil rights," the park celebrates her legacy of equality, inclusion, and community through recreation and shared public spaces.

Singing Hills Park is a 14.3-acre community destination that has served southern Dallas residents since 1971. Featuring athletic fields, trails, playgrounds, and a state-of-the-art recreation center, the park connects generations through wellness, education, and community programs. Singing Hills represents a new model for accessible neighborhood spaces.

Kleberg Park is a 47.2-acre southeast Dallas community destination offering recreation, outdoor spaces, and neighborhood connection. With athletic fields, tennis courts, a recreation center, and scenic natural areas, the park serves as a gathering place for families while supporting being outdoors, community programs, and local events.

Miller Family Park is a 13-acre community park honoring the legacy of a historic farming community founded by formerly enslaved people. Today, the park provides a welcoming space for recreation and connection while preserving the stories of perseverance, family, and resilience that shaped the land.

White Rock Lake Park is a 1,015-acre Dallas landmark offering scenic landscapes, recreation, and opportunities to connect with nature. Originally created as a water source for the city of Dallas in 1911, the lake has become a beloved destination for trails, wildlife viewing, outdoor activities, community events, and generations of memories.

Hamilton Park is a community park with tennis and basketball courts, a playground, and swimming pool. Established in the historic Hamilton Park neighborhood, the park honors generations of residents who built their neighborhood through leadership, recreation, and programs that continue supporting families and young people today.

Fretz Park carries the legacy of Dallas's first municipal playground, Trinity Play Park, which was established in 1909 to serve working families in the Cotton Mills District. Today, the park represents a century-long commitment to recreation, education, and community support, while preserving the history of creating spaces where children can thrive.

Campbell Green Park is a 17.5-acre community park established in 1974 that has served North Dallas residents for generations. Named after the historic Campbell family, the park offers tennis and pickleball courts, trails, a sprayground, bark park, recreation center, and gathering spaces that support recreation, wellness, and community connection.

Marcus Park is a 17.1-acre community park established in 1963 that has served North Dallas residents for decades. The park features athletic fields, a playground, picnic areas, trails, and recreation facilities, including programs for all ages. It remains a valued neighborhood gathering place promoting recreation, wellness, and community connection.

Tietze Park is an 8.2-acre East Dallas neighborhood treasure that has served local residents since 1924. Featuring historic architecture, mature trees, recreational amenities, and strong community stewardship, the park offers a welcoming space for sports, gatherings, relaxation, and connection throughout the Lakewood community.

Freedman's Memorial Cemetery is a 1.7-acre historic park preserving the legacy of Dallas' Freedman's Town. Originally established in 1869, the site honors generations of Black residents through a powerful memorial featuring public art, historic markers, and spaces for reflection, education, and remembrance.

Klyde Warren Park is a 5.4-acre urban park built above the Woodall Rodgers Freeway, reconnecting Downtown Dallas neighborhoods through innovative design. Opened in 2012, the park offers gardens, playgrounds, events, dining, and recreational spaces that bring people together while showcasing the power of transformative urban planning.
